_note: Compiled from the real TH-queries repo (Logscale/Graylog folders + Old_Falcon, which is legacy Splunk SPL syntax per the repo README). Two Logscale queries (AI-domains DNS lookup, browser-process DNS correlation) had genuine syntax/logic bugs in the source files -- fixed here: broken regex alternation, a typo'd field name, concat() swapped for coalesce(), and a bracket mismatch in the final groupBy.

logscale.description: DNS requests to a specific domain (parameterized query)
logscale.query:
//This query will ask for a parameter "DomainName"
#event_simpleName=DnsRequest
| DomainName=~wildcard(?{DomainName="*"}, ignoreCase=true)
| table([#@timestamp, LocalAddressIP4, RemoteAddressIP4, Computername, DomainName, HttpHost, HttpPath, ContextBaseFileName])

logscale.description: Saved one-liner: DNS requests to known AI service domains (ChatGPT, Gemini, Copilot) (syntax fixed: regex alternation was broken in the source)
logscale.query:
#event_simpleName=DnsRequest
| DomainName=/(chat\.openai\.com|gemini\.google\.com|copilot\.microsoft\.com)/i
| table([#@timestamp, LocalAddressIP4, RemoteAddressIP4, Computername, DomainName, HttpHost, HttpPath, ContextBaseFileName])

logscale.description: Correlate process execution and DNS events to confirm a browser process performed a given DNS resolution (syntax + logic fixed: typo'd field/param names, concat->coalesce, bracket mismatch)
Endpoint network connections filtered by source/destination subnet and port
logscale.query:
//Just replace source subnet, destination subnet and ports in the query
#event_simpleName = "NetworkConnectIP4"
| cidr(LocalAddressIP4, subnet=["0.0.0.0/8"]
| cidr(RemoteAddressIP4, subnet=["0.0.0.0/8"]
| in(field="RemotePort", values=[80,443,22])
| groupby([ComputerName,ContextBaseFileName,RemoteAddressIP4,RemotePort])

logscale.description: Geolocate logons by user or computer (parameterized), with country enrichment
logscale.query:
//Query will ask you to provide UserName or ComputerName as parameter
#event_simpleName=UserLogon
| Computername=~wildcard(?{ComputerName="*"}, ignoreCase=true)
| UserName=~wildcard(?{UserName="*"}, ignoreCase=true)
| groupBy([aid, ComputerName], function=([selectFromMax(field="@timestamp", include=[UserName, UserSid, LogonTime, aip])]))
| ipLocation (aip, as=IP)
| IP.country=*
//Countries to ignore, if any
| !in(field="IP.country", values=["RU"])
| asn(aip)

logscale.description: Impossible travel detection: same user authenticating from multiple countries within a time window
logscale.query:
//Assuming you are already ingesting AAD auth logs
#event_simpleName=UserLogon
| UserName=~wildcard(?{UserName="*"})
| ipLocation(RemoteAddressIP4)
//Adjust the span as you like
| bucket(span=60m, field=UserName, function=([count(RemoteAddressIP.country, distinct=true, as=CountryCount), collect([RemoteAddressIP4.country])]), limit=500)
| CountryCount > 1

logscale.description: LNK file execution from external/removable drives, excluding common office apps
Hunt for legacy/insecure authentication protocols (NTLM, NTLMv2, WDigest)
logscale.query:
#event_simpleName=UserLogon* "Login*"
| LogonType=2
| AuthenticationPackage = NTLM OR AuthenticationPackage= NTLMv2 or AuthenticationPackage = wdigest
| count(as=UserName)

logscale.description: Hunt for files whose names suggest stored clear-text credentials
User logons and workstation unlocks, filtered by user or computer
Detect execution of Wireshark on an endpoint

splunk.description: Search shell command history events for a user (legacy Falcon/Splunk syntax)
splunk.query:
event_simpleName=CommandHistory
| eval Commands=split(CommandHistory,"¶")
#replace the username with specific username if you want to target a specific user
| join aid [search UserName="*"]
| table _time, ComputerName, ApplicationName, UserName, CommandCount_decimal, Commands, CommandHistory, LocalAddressIP4, aip, aid

splunk.description: Correlate Outlook process with a subsequent browser process to surface links/attachments opened from email
splunk.query:
#Lists links opened via outlook.exe
aid=* event_simpleName=ProcessRollup2 FileName=outlook.exe 
| dedup aid TargetProcessId_decimal 
| rename FileName as Parent 
| rename CommandLine as ParentCmd 
| table ComputerName, aid, TargetProcessId_decimal, Parent, ParentCmd 
| join max=0 aid TargetProcessId_decimal 
  [search name=ProcessRollup* FileName=chrome.exe OR FileName=firefox.exe OR FileName=iexplore.exe  AND CommandLine="*http*"
  | rename ParentProcessId_decimal as TargetProcessId_decimal 
  | rename MD5HashData as MD5 
  | rename FilePath as ChildPath 
  | dedup aid TargetProcessId_decimal MD5 
  | fields aid, TargetProcessId_decimal, FileName, CommandLine] 
| rex field=CommandLine "(?<url>https?://.*)"
| table ComputerName, UserName, Parent, ParentCmd, FileName, url, CommandLine, aid

splunk.description: Office applications spawning suspicious utilities (powershell, wscript, wmic, bitsadmin, certutil)
splunk.query:
#Office programs starting unusual utilities such as bits and powershell
event_simpleName="ProcessRollup*" AND FileName IN ("powershell.exe","wscript.exe","wmic.exe","bitsadmin.exe","certutil.exe") 
|   rename ContextProcessId_decimal as TargetProcessId_decimal 
|  join max=1000 TargetProcessId_decimal [search event_simpleName="ProcessRollup2" FileName IN ("WINWORD.EXE","EXCEL.EXE","ACRORD*.EXE","plugincontainer.exe")
    | dedup CommandLine]
| table  ComputerName UserName RemoteAddressIP4 RemotePort_decimal FileName CommandLine

splunk.description: Script interpreters (powershell/cscript/wscript) spawned from Office/Adobe processes
splunk.query:
event_simpleName=ProcessRollup2 FileName IN ("powershell.exe","cscript.exe","wscript.exe")
| rename CommandLine as ParentCmd
| rename FileName as ParentFileName
| rename SHA256HashData as ParentSHA256
| dedup ParentCmd
#add also adobe acrobat reader
| join TargetProcessId_decimal, aid [search FileName IN ("WINWORD.EXE","OUTLOOK.EXE","EXCEL.EXE","ACRORD*.EXE","POWERPNT.EXE")]
| table ComputerName, TargetProcessId_decimal, ParentFileName, FileName, ParentCmd, ParentSHA256

graylog.description: Privileged AD group membership changes (Domain Admins, Enterprise Admins, Administrators) via event codes 4728/4732/4756
graylog.query: ((winlogbeat_event_code:4728) OR (winlogbeat_event_code:4732) OR (winlogbeat_event_code:4756)) AND (winlogbeat_winlog_event_data_TargetUserName:"Domain Admins" OR winlogbeat_winlog_event_data_TargetUserName:"Enterprise Admins" OR winlogbeat_winlog_event_data_TargetUserName:"Administrators")

graylog.description: Broad set of suspicious Linux command-line indicators (sudoers/crontab edits, reverse shells, history clearing, etc.)
graylog.query: (full_message:"/etc/rsyslog.conf" OR full_message:"crontab" OR full_message:"/etc/sudoers" OR full_message:"usermod -aG wheel" OR full_message:"visudo" OR full_message:"/etc/shadow" OR full_message:"/etc/passwd" OR full_message:"getent passwd" OR full_message:"rm -rf" OR full_message:"/bin/find /etc/" OR full_message:"COMMAND=authorized_keys" OR full_message:"viminfo" OR full_message:"COMMAND=/bin/python" "simplehttpserver" OR full_message:"COMMAND=/bin/python" "http.server" OR full_message:"/etc/sysconfig" OR full_message:"COMMAND=/bin/find /var" OR full_message:"COMMAND=/bin/nc" OR full_message:"COMMAND=/bin/socat" OR full_message:"COMMAND=/bin/python" "import pty" OR full_message:"777" OR full_message:"stop firewalld" OR full_message:"base64" OR full_message:"ns_sploit" OR full_message:"haxhax" OR full_message:"/bin/cp /bin/sh" OR full_message:"/bin/cp /bin/ksh" OR full_message:"ysocereal.jar" OR full_message:"/sbin/tcpdump" OR full_message:"insmod" OR full_message:"modprobe" OR full_message:"useradd" OR full_message:"lsmod" OR full_message:"wget" OR full_message:"/etc/passwd" OR full_message:"set +o history" OR full_message:"/etc/profile" OR full_message:"history -c" ) AND NOT process_id:777
